core_obligations: Choose an injective resolution F to I and use the definition of Rf_* to represent Rf_*(F) by f_*I in K^+(O_Y) (proof lines 2348-2350).
Compose the given morphism phi: G to f_*F with the morphism induced by the resolution to obtain a morphism G to f_*I in K^+(Y) (proof lines 2351-2355).

Apply the localization functor j_Y to land in D^+(Y); functoriality in the triple is the statement that this construction respects morphisms of triples, which the author leaves to the construction (proof lines 2355-2357).
proof_roadmap: Resolve F injectively and use the defining representative f_*I of Rf_*(F) (proof lines 2348-2350).
Compose with phi to get a morphism in K^+(Y) (proof lines 2351-2355).
Localize to D^+(Y) to obtain the canonical morphism (proof lines 2355-2357).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism of ringed spaces f: X to Y, a bounded below complex G of O_Y-modules and a morphism of complexes phi: G to f_*F, the lemma produces a canonical morphism G to Rf_*(F) in D^+(Y) and asserts functoriality in the triple (G, F, phi) (statement lines 2330-2345). The construction is explicit: choose an injective resolution F to I, recall that Rf_*(F) is represented by f_*I in K^+(Y), compose phi with f_* of the resolution to get a morphism in K^+(Y), and apply the localization functor to D^+(Y) (proof lines 2348-2357). The claim is H2: the content is the correct choice of representative for the derived pushforward plus the compatibility of the localization functor, which the author states in one sentence rather than spelling out.
